_README: GK sub-topic per question, keyed by bank question id (slug-qNNN).
The staged papers carry no section finer than "gk", so a
sub-topic can only come from the question's content. The
categories follow the taxonomy in PLAN-UDC-LDC.md section 5
(current-affairs, modern-indian-history, art-culture,
polity-constitution, geography, economy, general-science,
science-tech) plus mizoram, which that taxonomy makes a
top-level subject of its own.
Produced by a keyword classifier (prototype kept in
/tmp/opencode/classify3.js during development): word-bounded
matching with plural forms, strong words (one classifies) vs
weak words (three needed), the stem and options weighted in
full and the explanation's strong words counted as weak --
"Nehru" inside "Jawaharlal Nehru Port" must not turn a
geography question into history. Mizoram is the exception,
its vocabulary never appearing incidentally, so a Mizo word
counts fully wherever it sits. gkKind=current (the build's
own curated signal) counts as a current-affairs signal.
Measured on the 1,500 GK questions: 433 current-affairs,
386 general, 134 science-tech, 121 polity-constitution,
118 mizoram, 94 economy, 75 geography, 70 general-science,
57 modern-indian-history, 12 art-culture. Random-sample
audits of every bucket read correctly. Boundary cases are
inherent to keyword classification: a static award or
invention can match 'prize'/'invented' and read as current.
Regenerate, do not hand-edit: re-run the classifier over
src/data/banks/mpsc-udc-ldc.ts and overwrite the entries.
build_bank.py guards this file two ways -- every GK question
must have an entry, and every entry must match a question in
the build -- so a stale id fails the build instead of quietly
dropping a classification.
